scope: Six fresh two-turn conversations for a frozen rank-64 MLP16 plus rank-128 query composition. Prompts and budgets are sealed before the native process; no target text is used to construct either program.

cases.name: binding-reassignment-plain
cases.prompt: Remember this record: Mira has a red badge, and Niko has a blue badge. Acknowledge with OK.
cases.followup: Mira trades her red badge for a green badge. What color does Mira have now? Reply with only the color.

cases.name: binding-reassignment-list
cases.prompt:
Store these records exactly:
- owner: Ada; card: yellow
- owner: Bo; card: purple
Reply OK.
cases.followup: Update the records: Ada gives her yellow card to Bo, and Bo gives his purple card to Ada. Which card does Bo have now? Reply with one color.

cases.name: arithmetic-multiply-add
cases.prompt: Compute 17 * 23. Reply with only the integer.
cases.followup: Add 19 to your previous answer. Reply with the integer, then one short sentence explaining the calculation.

cases.name: arithmetic-subtract-check
cases.prompt: Calculate 31 * 14 and keep the result. Give only the integer.
cases.followup: Subtract 27 from the result you kept. Give the integer followed by a short check in parentheses.

cases.name: prose-label-example
cases.prompt: In one short sentence, explain why labels help someone find information in a notebook.
cases.followup: Give one practical example of a useful notebook label in one short sentence.

cases.name: prose-contrast-format
cases.prompt: Explain briefly how a heading and a date make a note easier to revisit. Use at most two sentences.
cases.followup: Now write one example note title and date that would make a recipe easy to find. Use at most two sentences.
